newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks in London slip on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks in London slip on profit taking.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks traded in London edged lower on Tuesday weighed down by weakness in Hong Kong futures and as players took profits after heady gains in recent days, traders said.

The Hang Seng London Reference index slid 52.11 points to 11,569.50 by 1417 GMT as interest worries in the U.S. resurfaced amid reports that eight of the 12 Federal reserve banks in the U.S. had requested a rise in the discount rate.
Earlier traders said positive comments from Intel Corp that third quarter revenues are running better than expected boosted Wall Street and helped Hong Stocks recover some early losses.
But shares slipped again as U.S. Treasuries and shares turned lower as fears of a hike in interest rates undermined sentiment.
"After the market closed in Hong Kong, futures were hit," said one trader. "People have become wary now after recent huge rises."
In Hong Kong, stocks climbed to close at their highest level in 31 months, buoyed by Wall Street's record highs. The Hang Seng index closed 53.71 points higher at 11,621.61.
But later September index futures, which traded on a near-par with the cash index for much of the session, slid into the close to end at a 30-point discount to cash.
Traders said there was little on the agenda for the remainder of the week, and players would continue to draw inspiration from Wall Street.
